challenge.notes: No records were extracted. This is a candidate-gene screen of COL4A1 and COL4A2 in Ecuadorian keratoconus families: 48 individuals from 15 families, plus 64 controls. Family KTCN-014 contributed 23 members; 25 affected individuals came from 14 other families. The authors conclude that no causative mutations were found, and that all coding variants are benign or common polymorphisms. They note that Gln1334His (c.4002A>C, rs3742207) in COL4A1 was predicted possibly damaging by PolyPhen but was not significantly associated with disease (p=0.056 within the family; p=0.17 in cases vs controls). The listed missed variants are the coding, UTR, and selected intronic designations printed in the text and Table 2. Table 2 contains many more intronic variants written with en-dash notation; these are also unrecorded. None of these variants is reported as pathogenic.

A curator might add a record for an unspecified de novo COL4A1 variant (1 proband, 1 family) with a phenotype of periventricular calcifications and colonic varices without portal hypertension, but there is no designation to string-match.

challenge.notes: This is a GWAS cross-trait (condFDR/MTAG) study of dermatomyositis and polymyositis, not a study of pathogenic COL4A1/COL4A2 variants. The only COL4A1-related variant is the intergenic DM risk SNP rs2084040 (chr13:110799415C>T, hg19). Table 1 lists COL4A1 as its nearest protein-coding gene. The text also states that an LD proxy of this SNP regulates COL4A1 expression as a cis-eQTL. No probands or families are described; the cohort is 1,131 DM cases, 1,094 PM cases and 11,697 controls. No COL4A2 variants are mentioned.

challenge.notes: This is a single-family case report. The variant was found in the fetus of the third pregnancy (the proband) and maternally inherited; the father is wild-type and the second-pregnancy fetus was untested. Counts of 1 proband, 1 family and 2 carriers are consistent with the text. The affected_carriers value of 1 is debatable, since both the fetus and the mother show phenotypes, but the text does not contradict the record. The only other mention of the variant is a lowercase form in Table 2, 'p.gly1417Arg', which is the same variant.
